claims.text: An outcome under Spec 046 states only whether the published sign lists concur on the identification of the drawn sign that Wells (2015) numbers 297 as a tiger.
claims.boundary: The scope is the drawn sign identified at step 1 and the four named published lists. It excludes any statement about what the sign meant in use, any role in inscriptions, any other sign's identification, and the correctness of the identification beyond the published record's agreement about it. The head proposition carries the identification-layer clause in this boundary: the statement is about that one drawn sign at the identification layer, with nothing else stated.
alternatives: the fragment could be read as a meaning claim testable by corpus statistics (refused by design D-18: an identification claim is checked by concordance, not by corpus statistics)
falsification_tests: the claim is falsified in scope if any Spec 046 output states a conclusion about meaning, use, another sign, or a population outside the four lists' record on this drawn sign

metadata.strongest_rival: the alternative reading in which a concordance outcome licenses a claim about the sign's meaning or use
metadata.verdict_rule: scope is judged by inspection of every Spec 046 output against this boundary; any output exceeding it is a defect of the output, recorded as such, not a finding
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C01 states what an outcome may state (identification-layer concurrence for this one sign); C15 states where an outcome is recorded (a dated first-check append beside frozen records). The two govern different objects - the content of an outcome, and its place on the claim record - and are consistent by construction: an outcome inside C01's scope is exactly one that C15 appends without editing any frozen record. Neither negates the other.

claims.text: The identification of the drawn sign as a tiger is the published consensus under the counting rule of F046-C08.
claims.boundary: Consensus is counted over the independent lists only (CISI, Parpola, Mahadevan); the source list (Wells) is scored but never counts toward the two (F046-C08). AGREE is at the tiger-kind level, the 'horned' qualifier recorded not scored (F046-C09). The statement is about the published record, not about the ancient sign beyond the identification layer (F046-C01). The head proposition carries the threshold clause in this boundary: CONSENSUS requires at least two published lists independent of the source scoring AGREE, with zero held or citable published lists scoring DISAGREE.
alternatives: the identification is one scholar's call (SINGLE-SOURCE)
the identification is corroborated once but not a consensus (PARTIAL CONCURRENCE)
a published list identifies the sign otherwise (CONTESTED)
falsification_tests: run the §5 concordance: if fewer than two independent lists score AGREE, or any list scores DISAGREE, this hypothesis is not supported and the outcome is recorded under F046-C10's mapping

The head proposition carries the gate enumeration in this boundary: the source book cannot be produced from the program held copy with the passage located verbatim; any of the four named lists (CISI, Parpola, Mahadevan, Wells) is neither held nor citable with a full bibliographic citation plus its own locator form; any spec section 2 input hash mismatches.

claims.text: Wells scores in the SOURCE role in the Spec 046 concordance.
claims.boundary: Independence here is publication-level: a list other than the source's, published under its own authority. It does not assert the lists' scholarly traditions are unrelated (spec §7); the freeze may add a lineage note before scoring, openly, but may not re-weight rows after scoring. If Wells's own sign apparatus contradicts his passage, the divergence is quoted and the outcome cannot be CONSENSUS (spec §5.1). The head proposition carries the counting clause in this boundary: Wells never counts toward the two independent agreements CONSENSUS requires, because the claim source document is Wells (2015) itself.
alternatives: counting Wells among the agreeing lists, as a naive reading of design D-18's four-list set would allow (refused: a source cannot corroborate itself; the design's own word is 'independent')
falsification_tests: the §5.2 count A is computed over CISI, Parpola, and Mahadevan rows only; an outcome record whose A includes the Wells row falsifies compliance

claims.text: Each list row carries one scored state from the AGREE / DISAGREE / SILENT set.
claims.boundary: Scoring is from the list's own entry for the drawn sign at its recorded locator. A functional or graphic description offered by a list as its identification of the sign scores DISAGREE, not SILENT: the distinction is whether the list identifies the sign as something, not whether that something is an animal. The source's own hedge ('horned tiger, or perhaps just 'tiger' generically') is one identification with a qualifier in doubt, which is why agreement is scored at the kind level. The head proposition carries the scoring definitions in this boundary: AGREE means the list identifies the drawn sign as a tiger, the horned qualifier recorded verbatim in place of being scored; DISAGREE means the list identifies the drawn sign as something other than a tiger, quoted verbatim; SILENT means the list gives no referent identification for the drawn sign, with the sub-state entry_present recording whether an entry for the sign exists.
alternatives: scoring 'horned' as part of the agreement test, so a list saying plain 'tiger' would count against the source that itself hedges the qualifier (refused)
falsification_tests: each row's verbatim quote (or recorded silence) at its locator either satisfies its scored state under these definitions or it does not; any reader can re-score the four rows from the published quotes alone

metadata.strongest_rival: scoring drift at the AGREE/SILENT boundary — a vague list entry argued into agreement because the outcome needs it
metadata.verdict_rule: rows are published with quotes and locators; the scoring definitions here are the only ones the outcome record may use

claims.text: The per-sign concurrence state comes from the spec section 5.2 mapping over the four scored rows.
claims.boundary: The mapping is total: every pattern of scored rows lands in exactly one state. CONSENSUS, SINGLE-SOURCE, and CONTESTED are design D-18's words, carried verbatim; PARTIAL CONCURRENCE is this draft's addition (DD-046-3), because the design's three words map no outcome onto exactly-one-agreement — the freeze may rename or re-map it openly, provided totality is kept. The head proposition carries the state definitions in this boundary: CONSENSUS (at least two independent lists AGREE, zero lists DISAGREE); CONTESTED (at least one list DISAGREEs); PARTIAL CONCURRENCE (exactly one independent list AGREEs, zero lists DISAGREE); SINGLE-SOURCE (zero independent lists AGREE, zero lists DISAGREE).
falsification_tests: the stated state must be derivable from the four published rows by this mapping alone; a state that requires any fact outside the rows falsifies the outcome record

claims.text: The Spec 046 concordance draws solely on published-list sources.
claims.boundary: This is the design's no-circularity rule: the concordance feeds the classification, so the classification cannot be among its inputs. The crosswalk registry is a matching instrument, not a classification: registry descriptions are used to locate entries, never as a list's identification of the drawn sign (that comes only from the list itself, quoted). The head proposition carries the exclusion clause in this boundary: Asset A material, Spec 045 depicted-kind labels, plus positional results are excluded; the only identification sources are the four published lists, with the crosswalk registry as matching instrument.
